invariants_checked: Stdio MCP transport is unconditionally disabled in both NewMCPClient and MCPManager.GetOrCreateClient, preventing arbitrary host subprocess execution or host secret environment inheritance.

Outbound service URLs, OAuth metadata URLs, authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, registration_endpoint, and authorization redirects are validated against SSRF/private IP rules and same-origin redirect restrictions.

MCP SSE and Streamable HTTP transports pin all requests (including server-pushed SSE endpoint events and mid-stream updates) to the configured service origin (scheme + canonical host:port) without embedded userinfo or fragments, preventing credential leakage on scheme downgrades or poisoned endpoints.
OAuth runtime refreshes on MCP clients validate discovered authorization-server metadata before posting refresh tokens.

MCPManager isolates cached OAuth connections per (serviceID, tenantID, principal) and isolates builtin non-OAuth connections per tenant, while rejecting cross-tenant access to non-builtin tenant-owned services.

HTTP JSON/error responses, OAuth token/metadata responses, and individual SSE lines/events are strictly byte-bounded while permitting unlimited sequential bounded events over long-lived SSE streams; concurrency and shutdown verified under -race with zero weknora/wk_ residues.

findings.summary: Upstream mcp-go SSE endpoint handling only compared endpoint.Host != baseURL.Host, permitting server-pushed endpoint events (at Connect or mid-stream) to change scheme (e.g. https->http downgrade) or inject URL userinfo on the same host:port and leak Authorization/X-API-Key headers.

MCPManager keyed cached OAuth clients solely by serviceID + principal.StorageID() without tenantID (causing cross-tenant OAuth client/token-store reuse on shared builtin services when a web user switched workspaces) and did not reject cross-tenant callers on non-builtin tenant-owned services.

findings.file: internal/mcp/security.go, internal/mcp/client.go, internal/mcp/oauth_manager.go, internal/mcp/oauth_assertion.go, internal/mcp/oauth_lifecycle.go, internal/mcp/errors.go
findings.summary: MCP HTTP JSON/error responses, OAuth metadata/token responses, and single SSE lines/events lacked byte-size caps (allowing host OOM via oversized responses or newline-free SSE streams), and NewMCPClient OAuth refreshes did not validate discovered token_endpoint metadata prior to posting refresh tokens.

invariants_checked: Every MCP tool call is gated by endpointFromContext, ep.HasTool allowlist, per-endpoint rate limiting, and tenant/KB/document scope resolution strictly derived from the authenticated MCPEndpoint context (never caller-supplied tenant IDs).

Cross-tenant knowledge bases, documents, agents, and wiki pages are rejected unless explicitly shared via organization KB shares, with owner-tenant execution context and Caller/TenantAPIKeyScope preserved.
All mutating document tools (add_document, update_document, delete_document) enforce access.RequireKBWrite(ctx, kb) before invoking KnowledgeService.

Inbound Streamable HTTP POST request bodies are capped at 4 MiB (returning HTTP 413 without unbounded io.ReadAll buffering), grep regexes and pagination limits are bounded, and spawned QA/touchLastUsed goroutines isolate panics cleanly under -race.

findings.summary: Published /mcp/:endpoint_id Streamable HTTP handler delegated directly to mcp-go StreamableHTTPServer (which runs io.ReadAll(r.Body) with no size limit), allowing oversized POST bodies to exhaust server memory.

handleUpdateDocument and handleDeleteDocument omitted access.RequireKBWrite(ctx, kb) at the MCP handler admission boundary (unlike handleAddDocument), failing to enforce APIKeyCapabilityIngest before calling KnowledgeService.

Spawned goroutines in runQA (KnowledgeQA/AgentQA) and touchLastUsed lacked panic recovery (server.WithRecovery only wraps synchronous handler goroutines), allowing downstream panics to crash the entire server process.

invariants_checked: Every REST path parameter across GENYEEClient passes through _safe_path_segment / _safe_wiki_slug (percent-encoded with safe='', blocking empty/whitespace/dot-segments/slashes/query/fragment/encoded-traversal/control characters before network I/O).

Local file uploads enforce O_NOFOLLOW + openat directory traversal via upload_paths.py, fail closed on remote transports unless MCP_ALLOWED_UPLOAD_DIRS is configured, block sensitive hidden segments, and eliminate outside-root file existence oracles.

Network transports (sse/http) require >=32-char constant-time MCP_SERVER_AUTH_TOKEN across both HTTP and WebSocket ASGI scopes, enforce DNS rebinding Host/Origin allowlists even on wildcard binds, and gate admin tools behind MCP_ENABLE_ADMIN_TOOLS.

GENYEEClient enables SSL verification by default, enforces positive request/SSE timeouts, refuses cross-origin or scheme-changing redirects to prevent X-API-Key leakage, and bounds both JSON API responses (32 MiB) and single SSE lines/events (8 MiB).

CLI entrypoints (genyee-mcp-server, genyee-server, main.py, run.py, run_server.py), pyproject.toml, setup.py, Dockerfile, and docs are consistent with GENYEE; protected MIT/changelog files (LICENSE, LICENSE.GENYEE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, CHANGELOG.md) remain byte-identical.

findings.summary: GENYEEClient attached X-API-Key to requests.Session headers and multipart requests.post calls; because requests only strips Authorization on cross-host redirects, a cross-origin or https->http redirect leaked X-API-Key to untrusted hosts or cleartext HTTP.

_iter_sse_lines accumulated bytes into pending without any cap until a newline arrived (allowing a newline-free stream to bypass MAX_SSE_EVENT_BYTES and OOM the process), and GENYEEClient._request read unbounded HTTP JSON response bodies into memory.
MCPAuthMiddleware bypassed token verification for all ASGI scopes where scope['type'] != 'http' rather than only 'lifespan', leaving 'websocket' scopes unauthenticated.

Non-positive GENYEE_API_TIMEOUT / GENYEE_CHAT_TIMEOUT integers (0 or negative) were accepted without falling back to 300s, and empty/non-numeric/out-of-range MCP_PORT values crashed CLI startup, --help, and --check-only.
